Initially, this Claim Petition is filed by the original Petitioner Ramkirtan Sahu against Respondents under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act seeking Compensation of Rs.40,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by him in a Road Traffic accident.
Subsequently, on his death, his Legal Representatives came on record as Petitioner No.1(a) to 1(d).

2. The substance of averments made in the Petition is as under:
That on 01.04.2020 at about 7.00 p.m., when the deceased by name Ramkirtan Sahu was proceeding as a pedestrian on the extreme left side of mud road and when he reached near SCCH 15 4 MVC No.176/2021 Rice mill, Bengaluru - Kanakapura road,
Kanakapura town and Taluk, Ramanagara District, at that time, one Motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-42-J-2984 ridden by its rider came in a rash and negligent Ram Kirtan Sahu vs Kempe Gowda on 6 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/104689822/

Immediately after the accident, the Ramakrishna Sahu was taken to Kanakapura Government Hospital and after First Aid treatment, he was shifted to NIMHANS, wherein he was treated as an inpatient from 02.04.2020 to 06.05.2020 and then he was shifted to Astra hospital, wherein he was treated as an inpatient from 06.05.2020 to 15.05.2020 and then shifted to DKS Super Speciality Hospital, Raipur, Chattigarh, wherein he took treatment as an inpatient from 22.05.2020 to 04.06.2020.

sentences.text: In spite of better and expert treatment Ramkirtan Sahu was not revived due to the accidental head injuries and he was succumbed to fatal injuries on 21.05.2021.

The Petitioners had spent about Rs.5,00,000/- towards medical expenses, SCCH 15 5 MVC No.176/2021 conveyance,
nourishment, transportation of dead body and funeral obsequies.
4. Prior to the date of the accident, the deceased was hale and healthy and he was working as a Mason and was earning a sum of Rs.24,000/- per month.
The Petitioners were entirely depending upon the income of the deceased.
Due to the death of Ramkirtan Sahu, the Petitioners have lost their bread earner.
The Respondent No.1 is the owner and the Respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending Motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-42-J- 2984.
Therefore, the Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioners.

5. In pursuance of service of Notice to the Respondents, both Respondent No.1 and 2 had appeared before the Court through their respective Counsels and Respondent No.2 filed its Objection statement to the main Petition.
After the death of the original petitioner Ramkirtan Sahu the claim petition was amended and amended petition was filed.
Thereafter, the Respondent No.2 has filed additional Objection Statement.

SCCH 15 6 MVC No.176/2021 The Respondent No.2 in its Objection Statement denied the age,
avocation and income of the deceased and and the accident caused by the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the offending vehicle and also the injuries and the death of the deceased Ramkirtan Sahu in the said accident.
Further it contended that there is a 9 days delay in lodging police Complaint.
Further it contended that there is no fault on the part of the rider of the motorcycle and contributory negligence is more on the part of the deceased.
Further, it contended that the rider of the offending motorcycle does not hold Driving License at the time of accident.
There is no nexus between accidental injuries and death of the deceased.
Hence, it is not liable to pay compensation to the Petitioners.
On these grounds, the Respondent No.2 has prayed to dismiss the Petition against it.
The Respondent No.1 did not choose to file Objection Statement.

18. PW.1 in her cross-examination admitted that in the Basavanagudi hospital her husband has taken only medicines.
She also admitted that as per Ex.P12 her husband taken only conservative treatment.
She further admitted that she has not produced any medical records of her husband after he discharged from the DKS Super Specility hospital on 04.06.2020.
Further, she admitted that her husband himself filed claim petition on 02.01.2021 and he himself put his signature on the claim petition and he has not made anyone to represent him.
19. PW.2 doctor in his cross-examination deposed that SCCH 15 17 MVC No.176/2021 they have not mentioned who has brought said Ramakirtan Sahu to the hospital.
They mentioned in their document as brought unconscious.
Further he deposed that when Ramakirtan Sahu sent to another hospital then he was on the stage of speak.
20. Admittedly, in this case, Postmortem was not conducted.

But, as per the decision relied on by the Learned Counsel for the Petitioner which is reported in 1993 0 Supreme (AP) 564, in between Khairullah @ Babu Vs. Anita @ Amruthalal Patel, wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court has pleased to held as under:
"Motor Vehicles Act, Sec.110(B) Motor Accident Death Compensation - deceased, businessmen and income - tax assessee lorry dashed against the scooter of the deceased who received multiple injuries and died during the course of medical treatment due to cordia recipiratory failure - Failure to conduct postmortem examination over the dead body of the deceased cannot be taken as circumstance against the claimants who are claiming compensation for death of the deceased - Remarriage cannot be taken as a ground to refuse compensation to the wife of the deceased."

sentences.text: However, in the present case in hand, the Petitioners have not produced single piece of document to show Ramakirtan Sahu after discharge from DKS Super Sepciality hospital on 04.06.2020, he was continuously under follow-up treatment till his death on 21.05.2021.
The last discharge summary i.e., Ex.P12 shows that he was conservatively treated and he got released on 04.06.2020.
Moreover, the Petitioner himself appeared before the Court by filing claim petition on 02.01.2021 and he also put his signature on the claim petition.
Further, PW.1 being the wife of the deceased Ramakirtan Sahu admitted the said fact in her evidence.
It is pertinent to note here that Postmortem was not conducted in the present case.

But, Petitioners being the LRs of the deceased Ramakirtan Sahu have not examined the doctor to Ram Kirtan Sahu vs Kempe Gowda on 6 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/104689822/

sentences.text: Hence, there is no materials on record to show the nexus between injuries sustained by the deceased Ramakirtan Sahu in the said Road Traffic Accident SCCH 15 19 MVC No.176/2021 and his death.
22. However, the Spot mahazar and Spot Sketch i.e., Ex.P3 clearly shows the accident was occurred on the footpath.
Though, the Respondent No.1 appeared before the Court through his Counsel, he did not file his Written Statement and contested the matter to show about the mode of the accident.
He has not challenged the Charge sheet filed against him.

Under such circumstances and by the oral and documentary evidence led by both parties, this Tribunal is of the opinion that the Petitioners have failed to prove nexus between the death of the Ramakirtan Sahu and the said accidental injuries.

Though, the Petitioners have failed to prove the Ramakirtan Sahu was died due to the accidental injuries, they have proved only the accident caused by the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the offending motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-42-J-2984 and in the said accident the deceased Petitioner had sustained injuries.
Accordingly, I answer Additional Issue No.1 and Recasted Issue No.1 "Partly in the Affirmative."

SCCH 15 20 MVC No.176/2021 23. Addl. and Recasted Issue No.2 and Issue No.2 and 3: All these Issues are taken together for common discussion as they are interlinked with each other and to avoid repetition of facts.
The Petitioners have proved that the said accident is occurred by the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the offending vehicle.
It is pertinent to note here that initially present petition was filed by the Ramakirtan Sahu for claiming compensation for the injuries sustained in the Road Traffic Accident.
But, subsequently, on his death, his wife and children and mother were impeladed as Petitioner No.1(a) to 1(d).
Petitioner No.1(a) is the wife, the Petitioner No.1(b) and 1(c) are the children and Petitioner No.1(d) is the mother of the deceased Ramakirtan Sahu.
It is pertinent to note here that this Tribunal comes to the conclusion that the said accident has occurred by the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the offending motorcycle.
SCCH 15 21 MVC No.176/2021 Hence, the Petitioners being the wife, children and mother of the deceased Ramakirtan Sahu entitled for compensation.
24. As per the detailed discussion made in Issue No.1, this Tribunal is of the opinion that, there is no nexus between the death of Ramakirtan Sahu and the said accidental injuries.
Therefore, the Petitioner No.1(a) to 1(d) are only entitled for medical expenses which incurred for the treatment of the deceased Ramakirtan Sahu.

sentences.text: Upon going through the medical bills and evidence of PW1 to 3, the total acceptable medical bills comes to Rs.1,64,171/-.
Hence, by rounding off the same, the same to be taken at Rs.1,64,200/-.

Further it is to be noted here that, when the deceased Petitioner was admitted in the hospital, he might have spent some amount towards extra diet and nourishment and for conveyance etc. which might borne by his family members.
Hence, by considering the period which he was admitted as an inpatient, it is proper to award compensation SCCH 15 22 MVC No.176/2021 Rs.15,000/- towards the said expenses.
Hence, totally the Petitioners are awarded compensation of Rs.1,79,200/- with costs and simple interest at 6% p.a. from the date of the Petition till the date of realization.

26. Regarding Liability : This Court has arrived at the conclusion that the accident has been occurred by the rash and negligent riding on the part of the rider of the offending Motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-42-J-2984.
In this case, the Respondent No.1 is the owner and Respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
There is no dispute about the validity of the policy at the time of accident.
Therefore, the Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to satisfy the award amount.
The Respondent No.2, who is liable to indemnify the Respondent No.1, has to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioners.
Accordingly, I answer Addl. and Recasted Issue No.2 in the "Affirmative" and Issue No.2 and 3 "Partly in the Affirmative".
SCCH 15 23 MVC No.176/2021 27. Issue No.4:

From the above discussion, I am of the opinion that the Petitioner No.1(a) to 1(d) are entitled for compensation of Rs.1,79,200/- along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of the Petition.

In the result, I proceed to pass the following :
ORDER
The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioners against the Respondent No.1 and 2 under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.

The Petitioner No.1(a) to 1(d) are entitled for total compensation of Rs.1,79,200/-
along with cost and simple interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of the Award amount.
The Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioners.
The Respondent No.2 being the  SCCH 15 24 MVC No.176/2021 Insurer, is directed to deposit the Award amount and interest within 60 days from the date of the Award.

ORDER
The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioners against the Respondent No.1 and 2 under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.
The Petitioner No.1(a) to 1(d) are entitled for total compensation of Rs.1,79,200/-
along with cost and simple interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of the Award amount.
The Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioners.
The Respondent No.2 being the  SCCH 15 24 MVC No.176/2021 Insurer, is directed to deposit the Award amount and interest within 60 days from the date of the Award.
The compensation amount awarded to the Petitioner No.1(a) to 1(d) are apportioned among them are as shown below:
1) 50% to the Petitioner No.1(a).
2) 20% each to the Petitioner No.1(b) and 1(c)
3) 10% to the Petitioner No.1(d) On deposit of the Award amount and interest by the Respondent No.2, since the amount is meager, the entire amount is ordered to be paid to the Petitioner No.1(a), 1(b) and 1(d) by way of E-payment after their proper identification.
The entire amount awarded to the Petitioner No.1(c) shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in his name in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank till he attains age of majority or 5 years whichever is later.
SCCH 15 25 MVC No.176/2021 The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw Award accordingly.
